answer: The chain turns two n-bit integers into their exact 2n-bit product in five stages, each feeding the next. (1) Radix digits (page vub): each input is written in radix 2^b with b = ceil(log2 n) and q digits, so the product becomes a convolution of short coefficient sequences, and the page shows that the convolution length S is large enough that nothing wraps around, and every coefficient is below 2^{3b}. (2) Address map (page guf): the map Phi sends a convolution of length S = s_1...s_d, with pairwise coprime axis lengths s_i, to a convolution on d axes by moving the data only with controlled shifts and axis reorderings. The page says this 'prepares' the next stage but does not say why the axes must be split, so I take it that the next stage works on each prime axis separately. (3) Resampling with chirps (pages roz, pap, dib): each prime-length transform is re-expressed through a power-of-two length t, with the source and target permutations left in place, so that only power-of-two transforms need a fast algorithm. For even t_i the chirp identity on page pap removes the target permutation: the transform becomes a chirp phase, a convolution of length T, and another chirp phase, so the permutation is absorbed into the convolution and never executed as a sort. (4) Twist to the polynomial ring (page taf): multiplying coefficient k of the last cyclic axis of length r by zeta^k, with zeta = e^{pi i/r}, turns that axis into the coordinate of the ring with y^r = -1; a wrap-around then carries a sign that exactly cancels the twist, so convolution along that axis becomes ring convolution, and the twist is undone afterwards. (5) Synthetic-transform convolution (pages tab and kur): the ring convolution over the remaining axes is computed from two forward transforms, M pointwise ring products, and the opposite transform, then scaled by M. Back on page siz, the scalings by S undo the 1/S normalizations, the result is multiplied by 2^{2b+4} S, rounded to the nearest integers, mapped back by Phi inverse, and carries are propagated to give the 2n-bit product, with total error below 1/2 so rounding is exact. The step from stage 3 to 4 and the claim that the twist is what makes the synthetic transform applicable are the weakest links; I followed the algebra but could not verify the cited error bounds.

key_idea.statement: Two integers are multiplied by splitting them into digits, placing the digit convolution on prime-length cyclic axes, computing it through power-of-two transforms by a chain of exact rewrites, and then rounding and carrying, with the accumulated error kept below 1/2.
key_idea.quote: The exact $2n$-bit product of the two inputs is obtained from the radix-digit convolution by the chain: radix digits, Lolazad to a product of prime cyclic axes, two forward source transforms (resampling and chirps), pointwise product, opposite transform, rescaling, rounding, and carry propagation, with total error below $1/2$.

reason: Answered with moderate confidence. The order of the five stages and the role each one plays are stated on the pages I opened (vub, guf, roz, pap, dib, taf, tab, kur, fam, siz; 10 of 15 page opens used). The weakest links are the reason the prime-length axes are needed, the reason the twist makes ring convolution applicable, and the cited error bounds in roz and tab, which I could not check on the pages.
